modern: His walk may be slow, but it is sure. He who hurries to get rich won’t be innocent or safe; but steady perseverance in integrity, even if it doesn’t bring riches, will certainly bring peace. In doing what is just and right we are like someone walking on a rock, for we are confident that every step we take is on solid, safe ground. On the other hand, the greatest success gained through shady dealings must always be hollow and treacherous, and the man who has gained it must always be afraid that a day of reckoning will come, and then his gains will condemn him.

Let’s stick to truth and righteousness. By God’s grace let’s imitate our Lord and Master, in whose mouth no deceit was ever found. Let’s not be afraid of being poor, or of being treated with contempt. Never, on any account at all, let’s do what our conscience can’t justify. If we lose inner peace, we lose more than a fortune can buy. If we keep to the Lord’s own way and never sin against our conscience, our way is safe against all comers. Who can harm us if we are followers of what is good? We may be thought fools by fools if we stand firm in our integrity; but in the place where judgment never errs, we will be approved.

notes.term: He that walketh uprightly walketh surely
notes.note: “But he that perverteth his ways shall be known” ([[Prov.10.9|Proverbs 10:9]]).

notes.term: He that hasteth to be rich
notes.note: “He that maketh haste to be rich shall not be innocent” ([[Prov.28.20|Proverbs 28:20]]); “He that hasteth to be rich hath an evil eye” ([[Prov.28.22|Proverbs 28:22]]).

notes.term: In whose mouth no deceit was ever found
notes.note: “Who did no sin, neither was guile found in his mouth” ([[1Pet.2.22|1 Peter 2:22]]).

notes.term: Who is he that can harm us
notes.note: “And who is he that will harm you, if ye be followers of that which is good?” ([[1Pet.3.13|1 Peter 3:13]]).

modern: This is the way to live. With God always before us, we’ll have the noblest company, the holiest example, the sweetest comfort and the mightiest influence. This must be a deliberate act of the mind: “I have set,” and it must be kept up as a set and settled thing. Always to keep an eye on the Lord’s eye, and an ear for the Lord’s voice: this is the right state for the godly person. His God is near him, filling the horizon of his vision, leading the way of his life and supplying the theme of his meditation. What vanities we would avoid, what sins we would overcome, what virtues we would show, what joys we would experience, if we really did set the Lord always before us! Why not?

This is the way to be safe. With the Lord always in our minds, we come to feel safe and sure because he is so near. He is at our right hand to guide and help us, and so we aren’t moved by fear or force or fraud or fickleness. When God stands at a man’s right hand, that man is sure to stand. Come on, then, you enemies of the truth! Rush at me like a furious storm, if you like. God holds me up. God stays with me. Whom shall I fear?

notes.term: I have set the Lord always before me

notes.note: Emptiness, worthlessness: anything that promises much and gives nothing. Not only pride in your looks.
“The LORD is my light and my salvation; whom shall I fear?” ([[Ps.27.1|Psalm 27:1]]).

modern: It is the height of grace that Jehovah should be in covenant with man, a feeble, sinful and dying creature. Yet the Lord has solemnly entered into a faithful agreement with us, and he will never turn aside from that covenant. Because of this covenant we are safe. As lions and wolves are driven off by shepherds, so all harmful influences will be chased away. The Lord will give us rest from those who disturb and destroy; the evil beasts will be gone from the land. O Lord, make this promise of yours good even now!

The Lord’s people are to enjoy security in the most exposed places: wildernesses and woods are to be like pastures and folds to Christ’s flock. If the Lord doesn’t change the place for the better, he will make us better in the place. The wilderness isn’t a place to live in, but the Lord can make it one; in the woods you feel you must keep watch rather than sleep, and yet the Lord gives his beloved sleep even there. Nothing outside or inside should make the child of God afraid. By faith the wilderness can become the suburbs of heaven, and the woods the entrance hall of glory.

notes.term: I will make them a covenant of peace
notes.note: [[Ezek.34.25|Ezekiel 34:25]], from God’s promise to be his people’s shepherd.
The personal name of God in the Old Testament, printed “the LORD” in most English Bibles.

notes.term: The Lord giveth His beloved sleep
notes.note: “For so he giveth his beloved sleep” ([[Ps.127.2|Psalm 127:2]]).

modern: A condescending picture indeed! Just as a hen protects her brood and lets them nestle under her wings, so the Lord will defend his people and let them hide in him. Haven’t we seen the little chicks peeping out from under their mother’s feathers? Haven’t we heard their little cry of contented joy? Let’s shelter in our God like that, and feel overflowing peace in knowing that he is guarding us.
While the Lord covers us, we trust. It would be strange if we didn’t. How can we distrust when Jehovah himself becomes house and home, refuge and rest to us?

With this done, we go out to war in his name and enjoy the same guardian care. We need shield and buckler, and when we trust God completely, just as the chick trusts the hen, we find his truth arming us from head to foot. The Lord can’t lie; he must be faithful to his people; his promise must stand. This sure truth is all the shield we need. Behind it we defy the fiery darts of the enemy.
Come, my soul, hide under those great wings; lose yourself among those soft feathers! How happy you are!

notes.term: He shall cover thee with his feathers

notes.note: Stooping down from a high position, in the good sense, without today’s sense of looking down on someone. A simile is a comparison.
The personal name of God in the Old Testament, printed “the LORD” in most English Bibles.

notes.term: The fiery darts of the enemy
notes.note: “The shield of faith, wherewith ye shall be able to quench all the fiery darts of the wicked” ([[Eph.6.16|Ephesians 6:16]]).

modern: The man God has given grace to live a blameless life lives in perfect security.

He lives on high, above the world, out of the enemy’s gunshot and near to heaven. He has high aims and motives, and he finds high comforts and company. He rejoices in the mountains of eternal love, where he has his home.
He is defended by fortresses of towering rock. The firmest things in the universe are the promises and purposes of the unchanging God, and these are the safeguard of the obedient believer.

He is provided for by this great promise: “Bread shall be given him.” As the enemy can’t climb the fort or break down the rampart, so the fortress can’t be taken by siege and famine. The Lord, who rained manna in the wilderness, will keep his people well supplied even when they are surrounded by those who would starve them.

But what if the water fails? That can’t happen: “his waters shall be sure.” There is a never-failing well inside the impregnable fortress. The Lord sees to it that nothing is lacking. No one can touch the citizen of the true Zion. However fierce the enemy, the Lord will preserve his chosen.

notes.note: “Behold, I will rain bread from heaven for you” ([[Exod.16.4|Exodus 16:4]]).
The city of God; here, God’s people and their home in heaven ([[Heb.12.22|Hebrews 12:22]]).

modern: There is no bridge: we must go through the waters and feel the rush of the rivers. God’s presence in the flood is better than a ferryboat. Tested we must be, but triumphant we will be; for Jehovah himself, who is mightier than many waters, will be with us. Whenever else he may be away from his people, the Lord will surely be with them in difficulties and dangers. The sorrows of life may rise to an extraordinary height, but the Lord is equal to every occasion.

The enemies of God can put dangers of their own making in our way, such as persecutions and cruel mockings, which are like a burning fiery furnace. What then? We’ll walk through the fires. With God with us, we won’t be burned; no, not even the smell of fire will stay on us.

Oh, the wonderful security of the pilgrim born of heaven and bound for heaven! Floods can’t drown him, and fires can’t burn him. Your presence, O Lord, protects your saints from the many dangers of the road. Look, in faith I commit myself to you, and my spirit enters into rest.

notes.term: When thou passest through the waters

notes.note: The personal name of God in the Old Testament, printed “the LORD” in most English Bibles.
“The LORD on high is mightier than the noise of many waters” ([[Ps.93.4|Psalm 93:4]]).

notes.term: A burning fiery furnace… not even the smell of fire
notes.note: Shadrach, Meshach and Abednego came out of Nebuchadnezzar’s furnace unharmed: “nor the smell of fire had passed on them” ([[Dan.3.27|Daniel 3:27]]).

modern: David had just heard the voice of the Lord in a thunderstorm and seen his power in the hurricane whose path he described; and now, in the cool calm after the storm, that overwhelming power that shakes heaven and earth is promised as the strength of the chosen. He who sends the lightning bolt straight to its mark will give his redeemed the wings of eagles. He who shakes the earth with his voice will terrify the enemies of his saints and give his children peace. Why are we weak when we have God’s strength to run to? Why are we troubled when the Lord’s own peace is ours? Jesus, the mighty God, is our strength; let’s put him on and go out to our service. Jesus, our blessed Lord, is also our peace; let’s rest in him today and put an end to our fears. What a blessing to have him as our strength and our peace, both now and forever!

The same God who rides on the storm in days of tempest will also rule the hurricane of our trouble, and before long send us days of peace. We’ll have strength for storms and songs for fair weather. Let’s start singing at once to God our strength and our peace. Away, dark thoughts! Up, faith and hope!

notes.term: The Lord will give strength unto his people
notes.note: The last verse of a psalm about the Lord’s voice in a thunderstorm ([[Ps.29.11|Psalm 29:11]]).
Sends the lightning straight to its mark. Unerring means never missing.
“They shall mount up with wings as eagles” ([[Isa.40.31|Isaiah 40:31]]).
